title: finding(tooling): the ported comment-mask corpus sweep runs on no PR — wire its FABRICATES-zero assertion into CI, and decide whether the port tracks upstream
body:
Filed by the `domain:devx @ objectui` execution seat (PM session `session_01FhBNJcLRZLe8M87VcUgpKr`, 2026-09-07T08:31Z) from the two open questions the #7882 dev left in its report (`5567331783`), after that card closed on its measurement. ⛔ No `domain:*`, type or grade set — triage's. Dedup: REST listing of all 452 open issues + local grep for `comment-mask` / `corpus sweep` / `lint.yml` (control `BLOCK_CONFIG` hit 5); no card covers either question.

## What exists on `main` since PR #8277 (`3c6394cb2`)

`scripts/check-comment-mask-corpus.mjs` (`pnpm check:comment-mask-corpus`) diffs `js-comment-mask.mjs`'s comment flag array against `@typescript-eslint/parser` over every source file (4,418 on `b6f821a8b`, ~33 s). Its verdict is split by direction: a FABRICATED byte (parser says comment, mask says code) is fatal; over-masking is reported against a declared ceiling (`KNOWN_RESIDUE`: 1 file, 1,517 bytes, objectui#7882's `DocsIndex.tsx` shape). Measured: FABRICATES = **0** today.

**Nothing runs it.** It is a hand-run instrument: not in `lint.yml`, not in any workflow, not in `scripts/upstream-port-pin.json`. Its FABRICATES-zero assertion — the direction `js-comment-mask.mjs`'s own header calls "worse than no verifier at all" — is therefore enforced on no PR.

## Question 1 — wire it into CI?

The dev's four-axis reading, carried here verbatim in substance: on the anti-AI-error axis the FABRICATES assertion is exactly the contract-tightening kind — it is at zero, so enforcing it costs nothing today and fails loudly rather than tolerantly; on the startup-focus axis it is a ~33 s step in an already-long lint job. It needs a workflow edit (`.github/workflows/lint.yml` or wherever the sibling `check:*` scripts run — read `scripts/check-entry-guard.mjs` and the Lint job's step list to see how siblings are wired), which no dev dispatch on this lane may make as a rider. Recommendation from the report: yes, as its own card — this one.

Acceptance if taken: the step runs the sweep and reds on a fabricated byte (ablation: plant a `//`-swallowing shape in a scratch file, CI red naming the file); the ceiling posture unchanged; `content/docs/guide/ci-cd-pipeline.md`'s Lint section updated in the same PR (objectui#8015 records that page already under-lists the Lint gates — check it before adding a fifth unlisted one).

## Question 2 — enrol the port in `upstream-port-pin.json`?

The port carries four structural divergences from objectstack's script (oracle reached via `typescript-eslint`'s re-export, a 15-line inlined prerequisite helper, this tree's skip list, the report-with-a-ceiling posture). The pin verifies by reversing declared divergences to a byte-exact reconstruction, which "would reconstruct most of the file and assert almost nothing while adding a re-sync ritual to every upstream edit" — so the PR left it unenrolled. Cost of that, named: upstream fixes (objectstack#16540 is the first — the port's own test found it) do not arrive on their own. Options: A leave unenrolled (today); B enrol and accept the ritual; C a lighter drift signal (pin only the upstream blob sha the port was read from, red when upstream's file changes — a "look at it" signal, not a reconstruction). The dev recommended A now, B later; C is this seat's addition for triage to weigh, not a recommendation.
